en: Applying sunscreen with SPF 30 blocks about 97 percent of UVB rays to protect your skin from sunburn.
When PAGASA raises Typhoon Signal Number 2, winds of 61 to 120 kilometers per hour are expected within 24 hours.
Washing hands after playing in soil prevents infection by hookworm larvae that can easily penetrate bare human skin.
Wearing gloves when handling pumice stone prevents skin abrasions because its highly porous volcanic texture is extremely abrasive.
Covering water containers stops female Aedes aegypti mosquitoes from laying eggs and spreading the dengue virus around your home.
Boiling floodwater for at least one minute kills harmful waterborne bacteria like Vibrio cholerae before you drink it.
Looking directly at a solar eclipse without certified eclipse glasses can cause permanent, irreversible damage to your eye retinas.
Astronaut space suits contain thermal control layers to protect the human body from extreme temperature swings in outer space.
Dropping to the ground and covering your head under a sturdy table protects you from falling ceiling debris during earthquakes.
Wearing an N95 mask during a volcanic eruption prevents fine, glass-like ash particles from severely irritating your lungs.
Evacuating immediately when heavy rain causes new cracks in hillside soil prevents burial by sudden, fast-moving mudflows or landslides.
Moving to higher ground immediately after a strong coastal earthquake is crucial because a tsunami wave can arrive within minutes.
